extracted.intended_audience: readers of historical biography and students of 18th-century European history
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter from a narrative historical biography (early life of Frederick the Great) mixing chronological account, anecdote, and critical asides about art, portraits, eyewitness narrative, and education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of pictures as 'reality' versus phantasms
rubrics_metrics.description: "Why it is, probably, that Pictures exist in this world, and to what end the divine art of Painting was bestowed, by the earnest gods, upon poor mankind?" (discussion that some paintings are 'phantasms' while others are home-grown, authentic, and of real worth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge paintings on whether they convey something authentic and memorable ('home-grown, just commencing business, who carried it far!') rather than merely fabulous or learned phantasms; tolerate mythic subjects in certain contexts but prize those visualities that arrest the reflective mind and have lasting worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer authentic likenesses over received pictorial-myths
rubrics_metrics.description: "The commonly received Portrait of Friedrich... is nothing but a general extract and average of all the faces of Friedrich, such as has been tacitly agreed upon; and is definable as a received pictorial-myth, by no means as a fact, or credible resemblance of life."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sceptical of widely accepted conventional portraits that are schematic averages; value likenesses based on sittings or contemporaneous observation and treat 'received' portrait-types as mythic constructions rather than accurate evidence of appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate reproductions critically (engravings vs copies vs originals)
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have engravings of this Picture; which are of clumsy poor quality, and misrepresent it much: an excellent Copy in oil... is now (1854) in Lord Ashburton's Collection... In the Berlin Galleries... few Pictures more agreeable than this of Pesne's."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely uncritically on cheap engravings or poor reproductions; seek originals or high-quality copies for accurate assessment of a work's pictorial qualities. Provenance and quality of reproduction materially affect judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value eyewitness testimony even when imperfect
rubrics_metrics.description: "Wilhelmina's Narrative, very loose, dateless or misdated, plainly wrong in various particulars, has still its value for us: human eyes, even a child's, are worth something, in comparison to human want-of-eyes..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat primary eyewitness accounts as valuable sources despite errors of date or detail; weigh them against other evidence but recognise the unique informational and human perspective they provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise definite visual certainties over rumor and garrulity
rubrics_metrics.description: "This of the Little Drummer, the painting and the thing painted which remain to us, may be taken as Friedrich's first appearance on the stage of the world; it is one of the very few visualities or definite certainties we can lay hold of... out of the waste Prussian dust-clouds of uninstructive garrulity which pretend to record them for us."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reconstructing early life or uncertain history, prefer tangible visual evidence (portraits, material artefacts) and definite facts over noisy, repetitive rumor or secondhand garrulity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for education: infuse useful knowledge and reject useless
rubrics_metrics.description: The paternal object and theirs being to infuse useful knowledge, reject useless, and wind up the whole into a military finish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing the Crown-Prince's schooling, prioritise practical and 'useful' instruction, eliminate what is judged irrelevant, and orient the curriculum toward the regime's goal (here expressed as a military completion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select tutors for practical experience, integrity, and conscientiousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of tutors: Duhan 'accomplished, ingenious and conscientious'; Graf Fink 'a gentleman of rather high solemn manners... undeniable perfections'; Kalkstein 'a rational, experienced and earnest kind of man'—presentation of tutor-qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose instructors with demonstrable practical experience, conscientiousness, integrity, and character appropriate to the pupil's intended formation (military/administrative). Personal esteem and long-term loyalty are positive indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dilettantism; seek what is worthy and memorable
rubrics_metrics.description: "...to the reflective mind, seriously loving and seeking what is worthy and memorable, seriously hating and avoiding what is the reverse, and intent not to play the dilettante in this world."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural appreciation and collecting should be guided by seriousness and taste: favour works with substantive worth and memorability and avoid dilettante superficiality or fashionable affectation.
